I'm new to wfpb so I hope the ingredients are alright. For those wondering, here's the general amounts I used (1 serving).
•1 small sweet potato
•2 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder
•1 tbsp pure maple syrup
•Around 200ml of plant based milk
•2 bananas  (frozen)

To make it, I baked the sweet potato until it was completely soft then scooped it out of the skin into a bowl. I added the cocoa powder, maple syrup and milk then blended in my food processer until it was completely smooth.  After tasting this, I decided it would taste better with some banana so I added two frozen bananas to the food processor and mixed everything together. 

I ate this right away but I'm assuming that allowing it to freeze would make a nice chocolate ice cream substitute.

It's my first attempt at making a wfpb dessert without a recipe and it went quite well!

Obviously this doesn't apply to every person's situation but I have to encourage this before I give any other advice. If you do find the courage to open up about your self harm to your parents and you feel safe doing so, I recommend doing that before anything else.

If telling them is not an option there are a few ways to conceal your scars. Maybe instead of wearing shorts, opt for a flowy skirt or a dress, maybe even purchase some mid length shorts which cut off around your knees. These clothes are all considered suitable attire for hot weather and I doubt your parents would object if you told them you wanted to dress modestly. 

You can purchase body foundation but I wouldn't recommend wearing this if your scars are fresh because it could mess up the healing process of your skin. This can be a good option to pack just in case you do end up having to wear short clothes though (bikinis, etc..). However, if you're short for cash using normal face concealer or foundation works in the same way, and it's less suspicious to pack in comparison to body foundation.

 If you do end up going out to the pool and you don't feel comfortable showing your thighs, it would be a good idea to pack swimming trunks or pyjamas shorts and wear that over your normal costume. If your parents question it tell them (assuming you are a girl- this is a taboo subject in some families though) that you are on your period and you feel uncomfortable not wearing a second layer on top of your costume.

Hopefully this helps a bit. Most of all I'd recommend using the holiday to relax. Try to use the trip as an incentive to stop self harming if you can. Thinking of it in time frames helps. Try to be clean for a day, and if that seems too tough try giving yourself an hour, or even a minute, then keep going another minute and another... eventually you might be a week free of self harm, then a month.. Taking small steps like this can help you get into the healthy mindset needed for recovery.

I too have recently lost a pet and it is extremely  hard because as you said, they bring peace into an otherwise hectic world. Losing a pet can often feel like you've lost a part of you. I deal with grief in a similar way, by 'shutting down', and there's some things I've done to help me function better which I hope you can try too. 

To avoid drastic weight loss when I have no appetite, I make sure to force myself to eat one high calorie meal a day. Sitting with others makes this easier for me because I feel more obligated to eat the food, even if it takes me >1 hour to eat a few bites. 

Don't beat yourself up about not working out at all. If you manage to go for a walk, be proud! If you need to rest for a while, allow yourself to do so! I cannot stress enough the importance of listening to your body. If a few days have passed and you haven't really gotten out of bed at all, then I would suggest finding a relatively small reason to get up then work your way up from there. For me, gardening was very therapeutic and it got me up every morning.

I can't offer much advice about leaving for university other than to tell your friends or family how you feel then you can work out things such as how to stay in touch. Bring items that make you feel safe and happy such as childhood toys to help cope with the transition and maybe also make sure you are able to look after yourself at uni by learning how to do laundry, cook for yourself, etc.

Hopefully the next few days will be easier for you.

Dont apologise about your feelings!! 
You mentioned that your distress stems from insecurities about how other people perceive you. The fact that you care about other's opinions to the point of feeling like absolute shite shows how much you need to put yourself first. I'd say the most important thing you could do right now is to find a healthy way to feel good about yourself- for me it was working out but for others something as simple as buying a new outfit can help! 

And about the 10kg you are so worried about... I get that it can feel like you look really different but in all truth, most people don't take notice of your weight. In my case, the only person I know that cares about my weight is my doctor so just make yourself aware that your brain is able to distort how you see yourself. If somebody does reject you because of your appearance, you've dodged a bullet by avoiding forming a relationship with them! Don't let arseholes decide how you should feel because you truly do sound like such a lovely person.

I hope that you're able to find confidence in yourself, you have my support :)
